task_reconstruction.summary: Project global language populations and geographic distributions for fifty years, recommend six multinational office locations and mutually exclusive language coverage, analyze fewer offices, and write a COO memo.

section_map.summary: Input: Globalization, geographic language dispersion, and sparse support data create a projection-and-office decision problem. Rhetorical job: Open with business stakes, reject a population-only baseline, and preview the complete two-model route. Analytical job: Separate language states, add migration and learning mechanisms, project to 2067, and pass the forecast to office optimization. Output: A three-paragraph summary that names the inhomogeneous transition matrix, data economy claim, forecast horizon, and simulated-annealing decision. Handoff: The introduction restates the two parts and the preliminary model defines the state system.

Input: The report begins from 6,900 languages, concentrated native-language use, multilingualism, and changing speaker populations. Rhetorical job: Convert broad context into two explicit tasks and a part-by-part route. Analytical job: Map transition-matrix projection to Part I and office location optimization to Part II. Output: A compact problem target and a two-stage roadmap with a forecast-to-decision handoff. Handoff: Preliminary notation and assumptions operationalize native and non-native speaker states.

Input: The model needs categories, state-vector indexing, transition symbols, and rates before any matrix can be interpreted. Rhetorical job: Slow the exposition to define who belongs to each state and what every indexed coefficient does. Analytical job: Bind native, non-native, learner, migrant, matrix, and rate terms to entry and exit mechanisms. Output: An operational vocabulary for the homogeneous state vector and its later extensions. Handoff: The assumptions constrain admissible transitions and double-counting choices.

Input: Overlapping language identities, births, deaths, learning, migration, exogenous change, and office coverage require explicit scope controls. Rhetorical job: Make simplifications inspectable by pairing each rule with an omitted rare case or operational consequence. Analytical job: Determine which state transitions, feedbacks, and assignment patterns are allowed. Output: A layered premise set for the preliminary, modified, and office-location models. Handoff: The N=2 transition graph turns the preliminary premises into a matrix.

Input: Native and non-native speakers of the same language are linked by births, deaths, and cross-language learning. Rhetorical job: Explain the causal transitions in prose and a diagram before presenting algebra. Analytical job: Identify self-loops, cross-state flows, forbidden entries, and the overlap that distinguishes this matrix from a Markov chain. Output: A four-state N=2 transition graph and the structural interpretation of Equation (1). Handoff: Eigenanalysis asks what long-run composition this homogeneous matrix implies.

Input: The N=2 graph, a steady-composition objective, and public demographic and speaker statistics provide a first model. Rhetorical job: Move from a small transparent matrix to a 22-language projection without hiding parameter assumptions. Analytical job: Define recurrence, eigenstructure, learning-rate allocation, population scaling, and parameter simplifications. Output: Equations (1)-(12), a 44-state homogeneous matrix, and a four-year projection procedure. Handoff: Table 1 and the long-run eigenvector test whether the homogeneous construction is plausible.

Input: Learning-rate sensitivity, 2013 inputs, 2017 observations, and a homogeneous long-run eigenvector provide diagnostic checks. Rhetorical job: Report agreement and deviations, then use an implausible limiting result to motivate repair. Analytical job: Compare predicted and reported speaker counts, identify data/model ambiguity, and test the homogeneous equilibrium. Output: Figure 2, Table 1, Equation (13), and the conclusion that time-varying mechanisms are necessary. Handoff: The Modified Model opening enumerates the exact missing processes.

Input: The homogeneous model omits learning duration, changing demography, economic change, migration detail, and English-speaker geography. Rhetorical job: Turn each diagnosed defect into an added state, block matrix, or time-indexed parameter. Analytical job: Add learners, migrants, English-specific blocks, exogenous drivers, and state-dependent annual matrices. Output: Figure 3, Equations (14)-(17), and a four-block English-specific transition system. Handoff: UN projections and learning assumptions instantiate the 26-language recurrence.

Input: Speaker counts, birth/death rates, migration, language families, policy/economic proxies, city data, and GDP histories feed multiple blocks. Rhetorical job: Explain data reduction and parameter substitution close to the model that consumes each quantity. Analytical job: Aggregate countries by language, compute weighted demographic rates, normalize attraction, classify similarity, and form office-region attributes. Output: Initial vectors, time-indexed rates, distance categories, candidate cities, and 2017/2067 economic inputs. Handoff: The modified recurrence produces trajectories and the rating model consumes terminal population and GDP.

Input: The 26-language recurrence, sensitivity settings, rating score, GDP scenario, and optimizer generate trajectories and assignments. Rhetorical job: Translate dense computations into rankings, plotted patterns, location tables, and bounded interpretations. Analytical job: Compare 2017/2067 rankings, migration and English distribution, and five-versus-six office alternatives. Output: Figures 4-8, Tables 2 and office assignments, and score differences for 2017 and 2067. Handoff: Strengths/weaknesses qualify the method and the memo compresses the decisions for the client.

Input: The attraction-share exponent controls whether learners spread among languages or concentrate on already popular targets. Rhetorical job: Define interpretable high- and low-uniformity regimes before comparing their curves. Analytical job: Change k from 1 to 0.1 and 10, then observe whether and when English overtakes Mandarin. Output: A modified learning-rate equation plus Figures 7 and 8 with a scenario-specific ranking effect. Handoff: The office application uses the baseline forecast while retaining sensitivity as an applicability boundary.

Input: Candidate cities, mutually exclusive language coverage, population, GDP, transport cost, setup cost, and language-load penalty define a combinatorial decision. Rhetorical job: Move from client needs to a scalar score, then disclose the search settings used to select an assignment. Analytical job: Evaluate city-language bundles with Equation (18) and search the constrained space by simulated annealing. Output: A score definition, 19 candidate cities, annealing parameters, and stable five/six-office solutions. Handoff: The 2017 and 2067 result tables compare alternatives and inform the memo.

Input: The optimizer reports five- and six-office scores under current and future transport/economic assumptions. Rhetorical job: Convert score comparisons into a conditional office-count recommendation rather than a universal verdict. Analytical job: Compare 43.0 versus 39.7 and 236.2 versus 225.2 while acknowledging omitted management cost. Output: Six offices are preferred in the scored baseline, while five remain a viable future option under a cost-compensation condition. Handoff: The memo states the same branch in client-facing terms and adds relocation suggestions.

Input: The finished model exposes interfaces, simplifications, state refinements, and remaining feedback/data omissions. Rhetorical job: Balance positive design properties with mechanism-specific limitations in parallel numbered lists. Analytical job: Separate extensibility and legibility from incomplete economic, migration-origin, education, and reverse-feedback treatment. Output: Four claimed strengths and four admitted weaknesses linked to future repair directions. Handoff: The memo uses the strengths to communicate results but should retain the limitations as decision boundaries.

Input: The client needs a concise 50-year language outlook, six-office assignment, preference cases, relocation plan, and office-count advice. Rhetorical job: Reorder technical outputs around executive decisions, tables, exceptions, and future actions. Analytical job: Compress model provenance while retaining scenario branches, excluded languages, mutual-exclusivity assumptions, and the five-percent claim. Output: A two-page memo with four forecast findings, three 2017 preference assignments, 2067 relocations, and a conditional five-office branch. Handoff: References and appendices provide the source and numeric trace that the memo itself omits.

Input: Six references, country-language mappings, demographic tables, alternative assignments, GDP projections, and additional curves support the report. Rhetorical job: Move bulky provenance and result detail out of the main flow while preserving anchors. Analytical job: Expose source dependence, units, scenario tables, and trajectories needed to audit main-text claims. Output: References, Tables 3-8, and Figures 9-12. Handoff: The appendix closes the evidence trace but leaves reproducibility gaps for data snapshots and code.

assumptions.summary: Every speaker-state identity is classified as native or non-native for each language, while one person may retain several identities.
Native states change through births and deaths; preliminary non-native states change through learning and deaths.
Rare first-language disability, instant language mastery, forgetting, and radical unforeseen structural shocks are excluded.
Selected matrix entries are set to zero to avoid the paper's stated offspring and cross-non-native double-counting paths.
Non-native groups share world-average demographic behavior, and target attractiveness is initially source-independent.
Learners do not reproduce as learners or die during the modeled learning interval.
Migrant offspring enter the native state of the destination region, and successful migrants leave the corresponding non-native state.
Initial non-native English composition is proportional to native-source populations, and native-English emigration is omitted.
One percent begins a foreign language annually; mastery takes three years within a family and six across families.
Six new offices cover 23 remaining languages mutually exclusively and collectively exhaustively, with English and the local language available at each office.
Population, GDP, transport cost, setup cost, and language load determine office value.
By 2067 the transport exponent falls to 0.1 because communications and transportation are assumed to weaken geography.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The report states about 6,900 current languages and uses concentration among major native languages to motivate a reduced state set.
Twenty-two of the top twenty-six languages are used in the preliminary model because of limited data.
Representative countries cover more than 90 percent of a language's native speakers before weighted demographic aggregation.
World-average death rate 0.0083, birth rate 0.0193, and immigrant/non-native ratio 0.172 fill common-rate assumptions.
A 22-value non-native speaker list supplies attraction weights but its printed normalization uses an inconsistent denominator.
Table 1 compares 2013-based four-step predictions with ten reported 2017 native/non-native counts.
UN fifty-year birth, death, and migration projections are reduced by weighted averages before entering annual matrices.
Language families are reduced to a binary same/different relation with difficulty multipliers 1 and 2.
Nineteen candidate cities represent the 23 remaining language regions after excluding English, Mandarin, and Wu.

Equation (18) uses population in millions, GDP in 10 billion USD, and an unspecified transport-cost index; raw Table 8 GDP is printed in scientific notation and therefore requires an undocumented division by 1e10 before entering E_ij.
Forty-six years of regional GDP history are said to fit an integrated four-cycle trigonometric projection.
The six references include a Wikipedia speaker list, four UN data endpoints, and a J.P. Morgan capital-market report.
Appendix Tables 3-5 retain country mappings, weighted birth/death rates, and 2013 native/non-native inputs, including missing Japanese values.

Appendix Table 8 records four dimensionless cycle factors plus 2017 and 2067 GDP for nineteen rows; it preserves source labels Rassia and Bengaladesh, and its second Spain row is probably Brazil rather than silently corrected.

results_trace.summary: Figure 2 reports a learning-rate crossing near 0.021 under the numerical bilingual assumptions.
Table 1 shows some close native counts but large non-native discrepancies, especially for Russian, French, and German.
The homogeneous long-run calculation claims a 0.9601 Punjabi native component and multiplier 1.0215.
Table 2 moves English above Mandarin by 2067 and brings Hausa and Punjabi into the top ten.
Figure 5 places English-region migration above 100 million and ahead of other labeled regions.
Figure 6 attributes more than 90 million projected non-native English speakers to native Chinese speakers.
At k=0.1 English remains below Mandarin in the reported high-uniformity scenario.
At k=10 English overtakes Mandarin earlier and reaches roughly 1.4 billion speaker identities by 2067.
The 2017 six-office assignment scores 43.0 versus 39.7 for five offices.
The 2017 six-office set is Tokyo, Bombay, Madrid, Rio de Janeiro, Moscow, and Paris.
The 2067 six-office assignment scores 236.2 versus 225.2 for five offices.
The proposed 2067 six-office set shifts Moscow and Rio de Janeiro roles toward Dubai and Jakarta but duplicates French coverage.
The report treats the narrowing future score gap as a reason that five offices may become viable after management cost.
The memo reports English growth, high-growth Arabic/Punjabi/Hausa, declining East Asian/Russian groups, and uneven migration.
The memo conditions a future office closure on saved cost compensating an asserted roughly five-percent revenue loss.

language_observations.summary: constraint-rich problem to model pivot: operating change -> specific obstacle -> why a baseline fails -> new model object -> bounded purpose; function=Move from a named practical obstacle or failed baseline to the exact model object introduced in response.; boundary=Name the failed assumption or missing state before claiming that a replacement is necessary; novelty language alone is insufficient.

part-by-part analytical route: stage marker -> author action -> model or data object -> result -> next-stage use; function=Preview a long solution as an ordered sequence whose output from one stage becomes the next stage's input.; boundary=A route is an organization device, not validation; every promised stage still needs evidence and a handoff.

operational category definition: term -> membership test -> entry mechanism -> retained identities -> excluded cases; function=Define overlapping population states by membership rule, entry mechanism, and exclusions before writing transitions.; boundary=Use only when the states are operationally distinguishable; explicitly disclose overlap and double counting.

assumption with mechanism and exception: modeled mechanism -> direction of change -> explicit exclusion -> reason -> scope consequence; function=State a simplifying mechanism while keeping the rare case, omitted feedback, or stakeholder constraint visible.; boundary=Do not turn an exception-bearing premise into a measured fact or universal law.

diagnosed limitation to structural repair: baseline output -> diagnostic conflict -> mechanistic cause -> required modification -> new state or parameter; function=Use a concrete implausible output or missing mechanism to justify a named modification rather than merely adding complexity.; boundary=The repair must target the diagnosed failure and be revalidated; a longer model is not automatically more accurate.

parameter source, transform, and role ledger: parameter -> source population or dataset -> transformation -> value and unit -> downstream matrix block; function=Attach each parameter to provenance, transformation, scale, and the equation block it controls.; boundary=A borrowed or assumed value remains distinct from a calibrated one; record missing units and normalization constants.

result anchored to figure or table: visual/table anchor -> direction or ranking -> number/comparator -> mechanistic interpretation -> scope; function=State an observable pattern, point to the supporting visual or table, and give a mechanism without silently increasing certainty.; boundary=Separate what the visual displays from the causal explanation; preserve horizon, unit, scenario, and comparator.

controlled sensitivity scenario contrast: scenario definition -> coefficient change -> held assumptions -> visual/result change -> decision implication; function=Change one interpretable coefficient, describe the behavioral regime, and compare the decision-relevant output.; boundary=Call this local sensitivity unless joint uncertainty, calibration ranges, and decision switches are tested.

conditional stakeholder recommendation: stakeholder condition -> objective weights -> selected option -> comparison -> review trigger; function=Tie a recommendation to client preferences, costs, horizon, and the difference between alternatives.; boundary=Do not infer economic superiority from an unnormalized score; show comparability, constraints, and omitted management costs.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The Summary names the failure of a population-only baseline, the added transition states, the 2067 horizon, and the client decision in judge-scannable order.
Using an implausible 96 percent long-run component to motivate an inhomogeneous repair creates a visible model-development rationale.
The application converts forecasts into an explicit office score and assignment constraint rather than stopping at language trajectories.
The two-page memo satisfies the stakeholder deliverable with findings, alternatives, exclusions, relocations, and a future review condition.

weaknesses.summary: Overlapping multilingual identities and non-unit column sums make the preliminary operator unsuitable for claims about unique total population or Markov probabilities.
The printed numerical matrix conflicts with its own parameter declaration.
The reported bilingual eigenpair is algebraically invalid and unnormalized.
The target-attraction normalization and gamma index conventions are inconsistent.
Large 2017 non-native errors are attributed to data without an error metric, alternative baseline, or recalibration.
The 96.01 percent Punjabi long-run claim cannot be independently checked and demonstrates homogeneous dominance rather than realistic equilibrium.
The inhomogeneous feedback timing may lag one period and several block symbols are reused or mislabeled.
Initial non-native English distribution is specified only as a ratio and native-English migration is omitted without a sensitivity check.
The one-percent learner entry, three/six-year duration, and binary family distance are assumptions without calibration.
The paper infers weak geographic influence from selected migration and English outcomes without an explicit geographic comparator.
The uniformity scenarios are mislabeled in prose and use three arbitrary k values without joint sensitivity or uncertainty.
The office score combines scales and treats a GDP/transport expression as setup cost without empirical calibration.
Simulated annealing lacks an encoding, neighborhoods, proposal and acceptance rules, seed, constraint handling, and convergence evidence.
The GDP cycle model omits its equation, fit procedure, diagnostics, validation, and uncertainty.
French is assigned to both Madrid and Paris in the 2067 six-office result, violating the stated mutually exclusive coverage constraint.

The 2067 result table replaces Moscow and Rio de Janeiro with Dubai and Jakarta, but the memo instead says to move Moscow and Paris to Dubai and Jakarta, leaving the relocation advice inconsistent with its own result.
Sparse references, Wikipedia-derived speaker data, missing retrieval snapshots, and the repeated watermark weaken provenance and reproducibility.

Tables 6 and 7 repeat a malformed coefficient caption; Table 8 prints Rassia, Bengaladesh, and a second Spain row that is probably Brazil, so the visible source labels must be retained separately from inferred corrections.

independent_extensions.summary: Rebuild the state system as a multi-membership population model with a unique-person ledger and explicitly conserved demographic flows.
Recompute every eigenpair and normalization from the frozen matrix and add residual, scale, and limiting-behavior tests.
Use rolling-origin backtests, language-specific error metrics, calibrated baselines, and prediction intervals before fifty-year projection.
Define contemporaneous versus lagged feedback explicitly and estimate block-specific time variation from documented series.
Estimate learning transitions from education and survey data with source-target normalization and uncertainty rather than fixed 1/3/6 assumptions.
Test geographic mechanisms with distance, network accessibility, policy, and migration alternatives instead of inferring weak geography from one curve set.
Run joint global sensitivity over calibrated ranges and report trajectory and office-decision switches.
Reformulate office choice with dimensionally normalized objectives, observed setup/management costs, explicit MEC constraints, and a Pareto frontier.
Archive a seeded optimizer with encoding, neighborhoods, acceptance law, feasibility checks, convergence traces, and exact-solver benchmarks on reduced cases.
Replace the unspecified cycle narrative with candidate GDP models evaluated by holdout error and propagate GDP uncertainty into office rankings.
